value.0: Hey there. I've seen you around town, perhaps you could help me.

I recently sent out a big'old shipment of Ale to Tharbad. Its been several months and no word back on payment or my men that went out. Course I fear the men have drunk all the supplies and staggered off somewhere. But ya see my boy was with em and leadin the shipment.

I know my boy and there ain't no way heed desert his dear old pappy. If you could find out what happened to him and the Ale I would be mighty grateful. I'm sure I could come up with something as for a reward if your interested.
Thank you much <FirstName>. I will be building my second shipement while I wait. Good Luck to ya.
Thank you again for finding my boy, and the shipment. I don't know how the missus and I are going to make it...
Hello again, <FirstName>. Any word on my Son and the shipment of Ale?
My poor son! *Sobs* Ahh my son!
Hmph. *Looks at your Sternly*

Thank you for all your hard work and toil. I owe ya. I have some gold tucked away. It was going to buy my son a trip to Gondor, he'd always wanted to see the White City. You take it. It seems right to me that you should carry it now.

You again, <FirstName>. *The Miller wipes his hands on his apron, and his eyes are old.* I owe you truth for truth: the boy you found on the Greenway weren't my only son. His brother Dob took the grieving hardest of us all -- fell in with a crowd of 'traders' working the Tharbad road, and now folk whisper they're no traders at all. Cultists, they say. Of the Red Eye. Find my Dob. Bring him home to me -- or bring me the truth of him, whatever it weighs.
Bless you. Ask along the road -- peddlers and bridge-folk see everything that walks the Greenway. Start at Tharbad Bridge, and go careful. I'll not bury two sons.
Any word of my Dob?
You're back! *The Miller goes still, flour drifting from his hands.* Your face -- tell me. Tell me of my son.

Home! *He grips the doorframe like a man in a gale, laughing and weeping at once.* The ale money's yours -- all of it -- and take the trading pack besides; it was to be Dob's, and he'll not need it where he's staying: home. You've given an old miller back his family, <FirstName>. There'll be a keg with your name on it come harvest.

*He is quiet a long while. The mill wheel turns and turns behind him.* Alive, and lost. That's a colder grief than the grave, friend... but truth is a kindness too, in its way, and you carried it all the long road home. Thank ye for that much.
I dont do chores.
What do you require Miller?
Go on.
Sounds like a fools errand to me. No thanks
I will find the Ale and your son. Take heart I shall return with word soon.
Good Bye for now.

Yes, I have terrible news for you Miller. You shipment has been befouled by goblins. And I fear your son has died at their hands. Here is the letter you sent along with your son as proof I found them.
Pull yourself together man you got no backbone.
Ah there, I might have been a little stern, but think of your wife now. She will need you.
Common Folk!
*Comfort the Miller*
Thank you for your generosity. Have faith good Miller. Fare Well.
No not yet. I will keep searching.
I'll find him, Miller. The truth or the boy -- you'll have one of them.
I've griefs of my own to mind. No.
Good bye for now.
Not yet. I'm still searching the Tharbad road.
Steady, Han -- it's good news. Dob lives, and he's on the road home. I talked the cult into letting him walk away.
Dob is coming home, Han. The men who held him won't hold anyone again -- their 'Voice' is silenced for good.
I found him, Han. He's alive. But he's... chosen them -- the Red Eye crowd east of Tharbad. I couldn't bring him back. You deserved the truth from my own mouth, at least.
Keep the mill turning, Han.
Be well, Miller.
